'''Mathematically Gifted & Black''' ('''MGB''') is a website that features the accomplishments of black scholars in [[mathematical sciences]]. In addition to highlighting the work and lives of established [[mathematician]]s in the [[African diaspora|African Diaspora]], the platform aims to support the next generation of these mathematicians as they pursue career goals in [[mathematics]] and mathematical sciences fields.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Mathematically Gifted & Black|url=https://mathematicallygiftedandblack.com/}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|title=Mathematics: Faculty Scholarship|url=https://digital.sandiego.edu/mathematics-faculty/1/|website=University of San Diego Digital USD|date=February 2017 |last1=Price |first1=Candice |last2=Higgins |first2=Raegan |last3=Graham |first3=Erica |last4=Wilson |first4=Shelby }}</ref>

Featured mathematicians must have a degree in mathematics that they use in their work and be recognized as a leader in research, education, industry, government, academia, or outreach.<ref name=":1">{{Cite journal|title=The Mathematically Gifted and Black Website|url=https://www.ams.org/journals/notices/201802/rnoti-p124.pdf|journal=Notices of the AMS|publisher=American Mathematical Society|volume=65|pages=124–126}}</ref> 

Founders of MGB received the [[Association for Women in Mathematics|Association for Women in Mathematics’]] 2022 AWM Presidential Recognition Award.<ref>{{Cite web |title=AWM Presidential Recognition Awards |url=https://awm-math.org/awards/awm-presidential-award/}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=News from the AMS |url=https://www.ams.org/news?news_id=7067 |access-date=2022-09-26 |website=American Mathematical Society |language=en}}</ref>

== History ==
Mathematically Gifted & Black was founded in 2017 by Erica Graham ([[Bryn Mawr College]]), [[Raegan Higgins]] ([[Texas Tech University]]), [[Candice Renee Price|Candice Price]] ([[Smith College]]), and Shelby Wilson ([[University of Maryland, College Park|University of Maryland]]). The professors created the website with the intent of highlighting the contributions and lives of black mathematicians. The name of the website was partially inspired by the song "[[To Be Young, Gifted and Black]]" performed by [[Nina Simone]] with lyrics by [[Weldon Irvine]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=About Us|url=https://mathematicallygiftedandblack.com/about-us/|website=Mathematically Gifted & Black}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Mathematically Gifted and Black|url=http://aammn.org/mathematically-gifted-and-black/|website=African American Male Mathematics Network}}</ref><ref name=":2">{{Cite web|title=The Voices of Black Mathematicians|url=https://blogs.scientificamerican.com/roots-of-unity/the-voices-of-black-mathematicians/|website=Scientific American}}</ref>

== Notable people recognized ==
Mathematically Gifted & Black features a collective archive called the "Circle of Excellence" that documents the website's [[Black History Month]] honorees that have been recognized since the site's inception. During the month of February, a prominent black mathematician is recognized each day, their accomplishments are highlighted, and a short Q&A with the recipient is often included. The mathematicians featured by MGB include university professors and a diverse variety of mathematical professionals.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Circle of Excellence|url=https://mathematicallygiftedandblack.com/circle-of-excellence/|website=Mathematically Gifted & Black}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Mathematically Gifted and Black|url=http://mathforum.org/library/view/78188.html|website=The Math Forum}}</ref>

Several notable individuals are included among the extensive archive of honorees. Their names appear below.{{dynamic list}}
